news_summary: Supermicro reported record Q4 and full fiscal-year 2026 results on August 11, 2026: Q4 revenue of $11.1B (17.5% GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.70) and full FY2026 revenue of $39.1B, up 78% year over year, on record backlog and more than $60B of new orders entering fiscal 2027. FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $65.0B-$72.0B. A July 21, 2026 preliminary update had already flagged unexpectedly strong gross margins (15%-17% versus 8.2%-8.4% originally guided) ahead of the full print. Set against the growth story, the same August 11 release disclosed that the company's Board is conducting an independent review of certain transactions in connection with export-control issues, which remained unresolved as of the earnings call. That review follows a March 19, 2026 U.S. Department of Justice indictment of three individuals connected to Supermicro (the company itself was not charged) alleging illegal diversion of roughly $2.5B of Nvidia-powered AI servers to Chinese customers, and Supermicro's own April 7, 2026 launch of an independent internal investigation led by two independent board members with outside counsel and forensic accountants. (The DOJ-indictment and internal-investigation details are drawn from a secondary legal-analysis source, not a primary DOJ or company filing fetched in this run, and are flagged confirmed:false accordingly.)

move_thesis: Supermicro's Q4/FY2026 print (August 11, 2026) confirms the AI-server growth story is intact: record $39.1B FY2026 revenue (+78% YoY), a large non-GAAP EPS beat, and FY2027 revenue guidance raised to $65B-$72B on record backlog and over $60B of new orders. That is counterbalanced by an unresolved, Board-disclosed independent review of transactions tied to export-control issues -- disclosed in the same release -- layered on top of a March 2026 DOJ indictment of individuals connected to the company and a company-initiated internal investigation (both reported here via a secondary source only, not independently confirmed against a primary filing in this run). With genuinely two-sided evidence -- a strong operating beat/guide-up against an unresolved legal/governance overhang -- sentiment is read as neutral rather than unambiguously bullish; the near-term stock path likely depends on which of the two narratives the market weights more heavily once the export-control review concludes.
